threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it ‘Stokey’ instead of the proper ‘Stoke Newington’ like the locals do. Even the pigeons seem to side-eye you for that.
Last night on the 196, a guy in a full tuxedo berated the driver for being late. Turns out he was late for a wedding he’d apparently just crashed.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I spotted a pigeon stealing a döner from a street vendor and the vendor just laughed. That’s Neukölln for you—chaotic charm.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg will you find a döner shop charging more for vegan options than the classic lamb. Just Berlin things, I guess!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by how they know to jump off the bus a stop early when BART suffers yet another meltdown. It's like a survival instinct here.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a bus driver calmly explaining route changes to a lost tourist, while a jazz trio played a lively tune on the corner. Classic SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all the locals love paella; in Gràcia, you'll find far more people loyal to their calçots and a good romesco.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the way they pause at every corner, checking their phones instead of just enjoying the architecture around them.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'Stokey' instead of Stoke Newington—locals know it's an unwritten rule to use the full name when you're proper.
Caught a night bus from Brixton to Clapham, and a guy serenaded us with an old soul song. Only in South London would strangers nod along like it’s a concert.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: It hit me when I saw a dance party break out in the middle of the street at Sonnenallee. No one cared about the noise, just pure joy.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you catch a Späti open at 3 AM serving fresh currywurst while a group of artists debates philosophy on the sidewalk.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local when they sidestep the dog crap on the sidewalk without even looking up, while newcomers are too busy staring at their phones.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a glimpse of a street performer directing traffic today near the Civic Center. Just another day of chaos in Muni-land, but the rhythm was oddly comforting.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia's plazas are just for selfies, but locals really gather there for spontaneous concerts and community events, especially on weekends.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their confusion over paella vs. fideuà—locals know you don’t mix the two for Sunday family lunch.
